sections.title: Discovery of an unexpectedly light and narrow beauty-strange state
sections.authors: LHCb collaboration: R. Aaij, M. Abdelfatah, A.S.W. Abdelmotteleb, C. Abellan Beteta, A. F. Abudinén et al.
sections.abstract: The LHCb Collaboration reports a new beauty-strange resonance with global significance above seven standard deviations, a narrow width, and a mass substantially below conventional quark-model expectations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the first observation of a nonconventional single-beauty hadron and interpret it as evidence bearing on chiral dynamics and heavy-quark spin symmetry.
sections.caveat: The paper is a fresh preprint; the resonance interpretation and implications for exotic dynamics require independent scrutiny and further measurements.

sections.title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
sections.authors: D.S. Akerib, A.K. Al Musalhi, B.J. Almquist, C.S. Amarasinghe, A. Ames et al.
sections.abstract: LZ analyzes 2.84 tonne-years of xenon data at recoil energies up to about 270 keV, finding one event consistent with a 248 ± 23(stat) ± 23(sys) keV nuclear recoil and a 2.6σ global tension with the background-only hypothesis.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a candidate event relevant to effective-field-theory and inelastic dark-matter models, while quantifying its global significance after look-elsewhere effects.
sections.caveat: The global significance is 2.6σ, not a discovery; rare background topologies and model dependence remain central.

sections.title: JWST evidence for a sharp "Cosmic Daybreak" at z = 15
sections.authors: Jiashuo Zhang, Tom Broadhurst, Tzihong Chiueh, Keiichi Umetsu, Hsi-Yu Schive et al.
sections.abstract: The authors argue that JWST galaxy ages and luminosities converge toward a sharp onset of luminous galaxies near z=15 and interpret this as support for wave dark matter with boson mass about 2.2×10^-22 eV.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a sharp “Cosmic Daybreak” near z=15 and say it is consistent with wave dark matter Jeans-scale suppression.
sections.caveat: The conclusion is model-dependent and depends on sparse, difficult high-redshift spectroscopy and stellar-population inference.

sections.title: Tension between MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE within a 3+1 Sterile Neutrino Framework using Simulation-Based Inference
sections.authors: Julia P. Woodward, Austin Schneider, Joshua Villarreal, John Hardin, Janet Conrad
sections.abstract: A joint simulation-based analysis finds that MicroBooNE reduces the MiniBooNE preference for sterile-neutrino oscillations, leaving a trials-based 2.7σ preference and at least 2.5σ parameter-goodness-of-fit tension.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim residual tension between MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE within the 3+1 sterile-neutrino model, not a sterile-neutrino discovery.
sections.caveat: The preference is only 2.7σ after trials, and the result is framework- and calibration-dependent.

sections.title: Broadband Quantum Optical Storage with Chemically Engineered Molecular Eu3+ Complex
sections.authors: Yisheng Lei, Senthil Kumar Kuppusamy, Idris Tlemsani, Suma Al-Hunaishi, Pengrui Jiao et al.
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally demonstrate a molecular Eu3+ quantum-memory protocol with 14.9% storage efficiency and 200 MHz bandwidth, designed to scale toward a few GHz.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a chemically engineered Eu3+ complex enables HAGEM quantum optical storage broader-band than existing Eu3+ solid-state materials.
sections.caveat: The demonstrated bandwidth and efficiency do not by themselves establish network-scale operation.

sections.title: Observation of the orbital Nernst effect
sections.authors: Yuto Masuda, Takamasa Hirai, Daegeun Jo, Naoki Yano, Peter M. Oppeneer et al.
sections.abstract: Measurements in titanium with nickel electrodes report a temperature-gradient-driven transverse signal attributed to orbital rather than anomalous or spin Nernst transport.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim observation of thermally driven orbital transport in Ti.
sections.caveat: Attribution relies on material controls and scaling behavior; separating orbital, spin, and anomalous contributions remains the key systematic issue.

sections.title: Disentangling spin polarization from driven circular ionic motion in EuTiO3
sections.authors: Clifford J. Allington, Matthew J. Lutz, Enoch (Sin-Hang) Ho, Fabian Graf, Martina Basini et al.
sections.abstract: Ultrafast X-ray diffraction and XMCD find large driven circular ionic motion in EuTiO3 without detectable transient spin polarization.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim circular ionic motion is not accompanied by detectable spin polarization in this system.
sections.caveat: The null result is material- and sensitivity-dependent.

sections.title: Achieving 5-angstrom-resolution diffraction contrast with an uncorrected electron probe and nanosized defect characterizations
sections.authors: Yao Li, Austin C. Houston, Ziang Yu, Zehui Qi, Siwei Chen et al.
sections.abstract: The authors report improving TEM diffraction-contrast resolution from about 5 nm to 0.5 nm using an equal-s condition.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the equal-s condition can largely replace the classical two-beam condition for defect studies.
sections.caveat: The method’s generality across materials, geometries, and defect classes remains to be established.
